slides.title: Lecture Overview
text: Previously, we mainly worked with scalar-valued and vector-valued features.
We call these features steerable features, meaning that rotation
𝑔 ∈ 𝑆𝑂 3 operates on them via matrix-vector multiplication.
Furthermore, scalars and vectors are called type-0 and type-1 steerable vectors,
respectively, to indicate how they differently respond to the rotation.

slides.title: Group
text: A group (𝐺,⋅) is a set of elements 𝐺 equipped with a group product ⋅
that satisfies the following four axioms:
• Closure: 𝑔 ⋅ ℎ ∈ 𝐺 for any 𝑔, ℎ ∈ 𝐺,.
• Associative: 𝑔 ⋅ ℎ ⋅ 𝑖 = 𝑔 ⋅ ℎ ⋅ 𝑖 for any 𝑔, ℎ, 𝑖 ∈ 𝐺.
• Identity element: There exists 𝑒 ∈ 𝐺 such that 𝑒 ⋅ 𝑔 = 𝑔 ⋅ 𝑒 = 𝑔 for any 𝑔 ∈ 𝐺.
• Inverse element: For each 𝑔 ∈ 𝐺 there exists 𝑔!" ∈ 𝐺
such that 𝑔!" ⋅ 𝑔 = 𝑔 ⋅ 𝑔!" = 𝑒.

slides.title: Example: Orthogonal Group
text: • the group of 𝑛×𝑛 orthogonal matrices with group product as the matrix product
• the group of distance-preserving transformations of a 𝑛-dimension Euclidean space
that keeps a point fixed (combination of rotation and reflection).
The special orthogonal group SO(𝑛) is
• the group of 𝑛×𝑛 orthogonal matrices with determinant 1 (subgroup of 𝑂 𝑛 ).
• also called 2D and 3D rotation group for 𝑛 = 2,3.

slides.title: Group Action
text: A group element 𝑔 ∈ 𝐺 operates on a domain 𝑋, i.e., a (left) 𝐺-set, by
the (left) group action ⋅ ∶ 𝑔, 𝑥 ↦ 𝑔 ⋅ 𝑥 ∈ 𝑋 that satisfies:
• Identity element: there exists 𝑒 ∈ 𝐺 such that 𝑒 ⋅ 𝑥 = 𝑥 for any 𝑥 ∈ 𝑋.

slides.title: Group Representation
text: A group representation 𝜌 maps a group element 𝑔 to an invertible matrix 𝜌(𝑔)
that linearly transforms a vector 𝐯 ∈ 𝑉 by 𝐯 ↦ 𝜌 𝑔 𝐯.
• Compatibility: 𝜌 𝑔 ⋅ ℎ 𝐯 = 𝜌 𝑔 𝜌 ℎ 𝐯
• Identity element: there exists 𝑒 ∈ 𝐺 such that 𝜌 𝑔 = 𝐈.
The vector 𝐯 is sometimes called a steerable (feature) vector [1] or a steerable function,
meaning that it is transformed by the group element via matrix-vector product.
[1] Cohen et al., Steerable CNNs, ICLR 2017
